topic: 学术综合任务与转段检查
grammarFocus: 根据个人错题复查时态、从句、冠词、数量和主谓一致。
title: The Archive Digitisation Project: A Mid-Point Review
instructions: 阅读以下关于一个模拟学术项目的材料，然后回答10个问题。材料中的情景和数据均为原创模拟内容，用于语言练习，并非真实研究或官方考试。请根据文章内容选择或填写答案。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。
passage:
A. When the city library’s local history archive received a small grant to digitise its collection of nineteenth-century maps, the project team expected a straightforward task. Six months later, at the mid-point review, the picture is more complicated. The team has scanned 1,200 of the 3,000 maps, but the cataloguing process has revealed unexpected problems. According to the project coordinator, Dr. Elena Marsh, the main difficulty is not the scanning itself but the inconsistent metadata attached to many items. “Some maps have detailed descriptions from the 1950s, while others have only a handwritten label,” she explains. “We have had to create a new standard and apply it retrospectively.” The team also discovered that about 150 maps had been stored in damp conditions, and these require careful cleaning before they can be scanned safely. This cleaning work has taken up more staff time than the team had anticipated.

B. The team’s workflow has evolved since the start. Initially, two staff members scanned maps while a third entered basic information into a spreadsheet. However, this approach led to errors: dates were sometimes recorded in different formats, and place names were spelled inconsistently. In month three, the team introduced a controlled vocabulary list and a shared template. Since then, the error rate has fallen by about 40 per cent. The coordinator notes that the improvement was not immediate; it took several weeks for everyone to adjust to the new system. “We expected resistance, but most people welcomed the clarity,” she says. “The real challenge was finding time to retrain while keeping the scanning going.” To address this, the team now holds a short weekly meeting where staff can raise problems and share solutions. These meetings have also helped new volunteers feel more confident about their work.

C. A second issue concerns copyright and access. Although the maps themselves are out of copyright, the library holds some modern annotations and photographs of the maps that are still protected. The team has therefore decided to publish only the original map images online, with a separate permissions process for the annotated versions. This decision has delayed the launch of the public website by two months. Dr. Marsh admits that the original plan was overly optimistic: “We assumed that everything in the archive was free to use. We should have checked the rights status at the beginning.” The team is now working with a legal adviser to clarify which annotations can be shared and which must remain restricted. This process is expected to take another six weeks.

D. Despite these setbacks, the project has produced some valuable outcomes. The team has created a searchable index of all 3,000 maps, even though only 1,200 have been scanned so far. This index is already being used by local historians and school groups. In addition, the project has trained four volunteers in digitisation techniques, two of whom have since found paid work in other archives. The mid-point review recommends extending the project by four months to complete the scanning and to develop educational resources for schools. The funding body will make a decision next month. If the extension is approved, the team plans to recruit two additional part-time staff to help with the remaining scanning.

E. Looking ahead, the team plans to focus on quality control rather than speed. Each scanned map will be checked against the original by a second person, and any discrepancies will be logged and corrected. Dr. Marsh believes that this slower approach will ultimately save time: “If we rush now, we will spend years fixing mistakes later. It is better to do it properly once.” The project’s final report, due at the end of next year, will include a detailed evaluation of the digitisation process and recommendations for other small archives considering similar work. The report will also include a section on the cost of cleaning damaged maps, which the team hopes will help other archives plan their budgets more realistically.

questions.prompt: What is the main difficulty the team has faced according to Dr. Marsh?
options: The scanning equipment is too slow.
Many maps have inconsistent metadata.
The grant money was insufficient.
The maps are too fragile to handle.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确指出，主要困难不是扫描本身，而是许多条目附带的元数据不一致。
questions.evidence: the main difficulty is not the scanning itself but the inconsistent metadata attached to many items

questions.prompt: What happened after the team introduced a controlled vocabulary list and a shared template?
options: The error rate fell by about 40 per cent.
The scanning process stopped for several weeks.
The volunteers refused to use the new system.
The project was extended by four months.
answers: The error rate fell by about 40 per cent.
questions.explanation: 第二段提到，引入受控词表和共享模板后，错误率下降了约40%。
questions.evidence: Since then, the error rate has fallen by about 40 per cent.

questions.prompt: Why has the launch of the public website been delayed?
options: The team has not finished scanning all the maps.
The library lost the grant funding.
Some modern annotations and photographs are still protected by copyright.
The volunteers need more training.
answers: Some modern annotations and photographs are still protected by copyright.
questions.explanation: 第三段说明，由于图书馆持有的一些现代注释和照片仍受版权保护，团队决定只在线发布原始地图图像，这导致网站发布延迟两个月。
questions.evidence: the library holds some modern annotations and photographs of the maps that are still protected

questions.prompt: What does Dr. Marsh admit about the original plan?
options: It was too expensive.
It was overly optimistic about copyright.
It did not include enough staff.
It ignored the need for a searchable index.
answers: It was overly optimistic about copyright.
questions.explanation: 第三段中Dr. Marsh承认原计划过于乐观，他们假设档案中所有内容都可以免费使用，本应在开始时检查权利状态。
questions.evidence: Dr. Marsh admits that the original plan was overly optimistic: “We assumed that everything in the archive was free to use. We should have checked the rights status at the beginning.”

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the searchable index?
options: It covers only the 1,200 scanned maps.
It was created after all maps were scanned.
It is already being used by local historians and school groups.
It will be published next month.
answers: It is already being used by local historians and school groups.
questions.explanation: 第四段指出，团队已经创建了所有3000张地图的可搜索索引，并且该索引已被当地历史学家和学校团体使用。
questions.evidence: This index is already being used by local historians and school groups.

questions.prompt: What does the mid-point review recommend?
options: Hiring more paid staff.
Extending the project by four months.
Abandoning the digitisation of annotated maps.
Reducing the number of maps to be scanned.
answers: Extending the project by four months.
questions.explanation: 第四段最后提到，中期评审建议将项目延长四个月，以完成扫描并为学校开发教育资源。
questions.evidence: The mid-point review recommends extending the project by four months to complete the scanning and to develop educational resources for schools.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what will happen to each scanned map in the future?
options: It will be scanned again at higher resolution.
It will be checked against the original by a second person.
It will be published without any annotations.
It will be sent to other archives for training.
answers: It will be checked against the original by a second person.
questions.explanation: 第五段说明，团队计划注重质量控制，每张扫描地图将由第二个人对照原件进行检查。
questions.evidence: Each scanned map will be checked against the original by a second person

questions.prompt: Why does Dr. Marsh believe the slower approach will save time?
options: Because it will require fewer staff.
Because it will avoid years of fixing mistakes later.
Because the funding body prefers slower projects.
Because volunteers work faster when not rushed.
answers: Because it will avoid years of fixing mistakes later.

grammar.title: 时态、从句、冠词、数量与主谓一致复习
grammar.explanation: 本部分针对你在错题复查中常见的语法点进行练习。请先理解句意，再选择正确的形式。注意：时态要与时间状语一致；从句要有合适的关系词；冠词要区分特指与泛指；数量表达要匹配可数或不可数名词；主谓一致要确保谓语与主语在人称和数上一致。
grammar.example: The team has scanned 1,200 of the 3,000 maps, but the cataloguing process has revealed unexpected problems.

questions.prompt: By the end of next month, the team ______ the scanning of all maps.
options: will complete
will have completed
completes
has completed
questions.explanation: “By the end of next month”表示将来某一时间之前完成的动作，应用将来完成时。

questions.prompt: The library, ______ holds many rare maps, is located in the city centre.
options: which
who
where
that
questions.explanation: 非限制性定语从句修饰物，关系词用which，不能用that。

questions.prompt: She is ______ honest researcher, and she always checks her sources.
options: a
an
the
（不填）
questions.explanation: honest以元音音素开头，表示“一个”用不定冠词an。

questions.prompt: The number of volunteers ______ increased since last year.
options: have
has
are
were
questions.explanation: “The number of + 复数名词”作主语时，谓语动词用单数。
